newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Yilmaz vows to fend off Islamists.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Yilmaz vows to fend off Islamists.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz vowed on Wednesday not to bow to Islamist pressure to scrap religious education changes at the centre of a dispute between the country's Islamists and secularists.
"The government is completely committed to carrying out the education reforms," Yilmaz told a news conference in parliament.
Police using dogs, water cannon and batons on Tuesday broke up a large Islamist demonstration in Ankara against plans to curtail religious high schools.
Yilmaz said Islamist strong-arm tactics would get nowhere.
"They are mistaken if they think they can intimidate the republic's government with street protests, threats and blackmail," he said.
Yilmaz, a conservative, came to power in June after Islamist predecessor Necmettin Erbakan resigned under pressure from the secularist army.
The new left-right coalition plans to extend compulsory secularist education to eight years from the current five, in a bill that would effectively close many religious schools.

Yilmaz accused Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party of using religious schools, known as Imam Hatips, to raise supporters. "The Welfare Party wants to protect these institutions, which produce militants for it," he said.
A government bill outlining the education changes is due to be voted on in parliament in the coming weeks.
